title: [CVSS 8.8 HIGH] CVE-2026-120698 — Wiki.js is an open source wiki app built on Node.js. Prior to 2.5.315, an authen…

Additional administrators with IDs greater than 2 can also be deactivated or deleted. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.315.

title: [CVSS 8.7 HIGH] CVE-2026-120697 — Wiki.js is an open source wiki app built on Node.js. Prior to 2.5.315, an authen…

The sanitized output is inserted as rendered page HTML and later compiled by the Vue 2 runtime compiler, so the expressions execute in the Wiki.js origin when another user views the page even when the author lacks write:scripts and administrative permissions. The script runs with the viewer's browser session and can read same-origin data, modify displayed content, present phishing content, or perform actions available to that viewer, including privileged GraphQL operations when a privileged user opens the page. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.315.

title: [CVSS 8.0 HIGH] CVE-2026-111760 — Git is a fast, scalable, distributed revision control system with an unusually r…

title: [CVSS 8.5 HIGH] CVE-2026-129784 — The httpx Ruby gem parses JSON response bodies through its transcoder layer. HTT…
summary: The httpx Ruby gem parses JSON response bodies through its transcoder layer. HTTPX::Response#json delegates to Transcoder::JSON.decode, and when the oj gem is loaded and multi_json is absent, the decoder falls back to json_load, which calls Oj.load(response.to_s) with no mode option. Oj.load defaults to :object mode, in which a response document can allocate any already-loaded Ruby class ("^o":"ClassName") and set its instance variables, or resolve a class or module reference ("^c":"Name"). An attacker who controls, or can influence, the URL an application fetches with HTTPX.get(url).json therefore controls object instantiation in the victim process. With a matching gadget chain, this issue can potentially cause remote code execution. Affects httpx 1.9.0; fixed in 1.9.1.

summary: The "Protected file patterns" setting of a branch protection rule was checked against file names as git prints them, and git quotes names that contain a double quote, a backslash or a control character. Such names never matched a pattern, so a user with write access could add or change files under a protected pattern by direct push or through a pull request merge, and could move a protected file out of the pattern's reach by renaming it. Where the patterns protect workflow files, this allowed adding a workflow that then ran on the repository's runners. Changed files are now listed unquoted, and a rename reports both the old and the new path.

title: [CVSS 8.2 HIGH] CVE-2026-68905 — Hugo Blog is a tech blog site. In commit 744ca15 and prior, the AI assistant pro…
